articles.4: Both: employers and workers must adhere to Sharia when applying the Law.
articles.6: Both: incidental, seasonal and temporary workers are subject to the same 9 listed areas (duties and discipline; maximum hours; daily/weekly rest; overtime; official holidays; safety rules; occupational health; work injuries and compensation; Minister's decisions). All 9 present on both sides.
articles.26: Both: clause 1 Saudization duties (attract, employ, retain, guide/train/qualify); clause 2 Saudi workers at least 75% of the workforce; Minister may reduce the share temporarily when qualified nationals are unavailable.
articles.29: Both: an employer must re-employ a worker whose work injury reduces capacity but permits other work, in a suitable job at that job's wage; injury compensation is preserved. Nuance: EN 'another job' leaves implicit the AR 'other than his previous work'.
articles.32: Both: recruitment from abroad for work requires Ministry approval.
articles.38: Both: no employment outside the profession on the work permit; worker may not change profession before legal procedures.
articles.45: Both: defines the qualification/training contract binding the employer to prepare a person for a specific profession. Nuance: AR 'qualify or train', EN 'train and qualify'.
articles.49: Both: training contract subject to 7 listed areas (annual leave; official holidays; maximum hours; daily/weekly rest; occupational safety and health; work injuries and conditions; Minister's decisions).
articles.59: Both: monthly-paid worker may not be moved to daily/weekly/piecework/hourly pay without written consent; acquired rights preserved.
articles.65: Both: worker duties beyond the Law - six numbered items (work per instructions; care of employer property; conduct; help in disasters without extra pay; medical examinations; confidentiality).
articles.70: Both: no penalty for off-site acts unless work-related; fine per violation max five days' wage; one penalty per violation; deductions max five days' wage per month; unpaid suspension max five days per month.
articles.89: Both: Council of Ministers may set a minimum wage on the Minister's proposal.
articles.92: Both: no deductions without written consent except six numbered cases (10% loan cap; social insurance; savings fund; housing scheme; fines/damages; court judgment capped at one quarter), with alimony first.
articles.108: Both: Articles 98 and 101 do not apply to four numbered cases (senior management; preparatory/supplementary work; intermittent work; guards and cleaners except civil security guards); Regulations set jobs and maximum hours for items 2-4.
articles.120: Both: Minister issues rules for part-time work; the Law applies only as the Minister decides, except occupational safety/health and work-injury protection.
articles.132: Both: this Chapter does not cover establishments that fall under the occupational-hazards branch of social insurance.
articles.134: Both: work injury as defined by the Social Insurance Law; occupational diseases count as work injuries; date of first medical diagnosis counts as the injury date.
articles.138: Both: permanent total disability or death gives compensation of 3 years' wages with a 54,000-riyal minimum (AR in words); partial disability gives the assessed percentage per the approved disability guide times the total-disability amount.
articles.154: Both: after maternity leave, nursing break(s) totalling at most 1 hour per day, in addition to general rest periods, counted as working time, with no wage reduction.
articles.158: Both: in all occupations and places employing women, the employer provides seats for their rest.
articles.161: Both: minors barred from hazardous or harmful work endangering health, safety or morals; the Minister specifies such work by decision.
articles.162: Both: clause 1 minimum age 15 (Minister may raise it); clause 2 exception for ages 13-15 in light work subject to sub-clauses 2/1 (EN 2.1) no harm to health or growth and 2/2 (EN 2.2) no hindrance to schooling or training.
articles.163: Both: minors may not work during a night period of at least 12 consecutive hours (AR in words), except as the Minister decides.
articles.188: Both: actual underground work at most 7 hours per day; presence at the workplace at most 10 hours per day (AR in words), including underground travel time.
articles.191: Both: the employer or responsible manager issues a list of public-safety orders and instructions.
articles.201: Both: inspector may order changes to equipment/machinery operating rules within set deadlines for health and safety, and may require immediate measures against an imminent hazard.
articles.202: Both: inspector keeps complaints about equipment shortages or violations absolutely confidential and must not reveal their existence to the employer or representative.
articles.204: Both: physicians, engineers, chemists and occupational safety and health specialists join inspections as needed; labor office director and inspectors may ask competent executive bodies for assistance.
articles.244: Both: supersedes the Labor and Workers Law (Royal Decree M/21 dated 6/9/1389H); repeals conflicting provisions; earlier regulations remain until amended.
articles.245: Both: published in the Official Gazette; in force 180 days after publication (AR in words).
